The Orange-spotted spinefoot Siganus guttatus is a commercially significant rabbitfish inhabiting coastal reefs and estuaries across the Indo-West Pacific region. Detailed life-history investigations reveal that this species attains a maximum recorded total length of 42 centimeters [Li = 42 centimeters], a size typical among larger siganids. During a comprehensive laboratory rearing study conducted at a stable water temperature of 28.7 °C [T = 28.7 °C], the incubation period from fertilisation to hatching was observed to be 2.5 days [ab = 2.5 days]. Newly hatched yolk-sac larvae were minuscule, with an estimated wet weight at birth of 0.000087 grams [Wwb = 0.000087 grams], reflecting the small diameter of the pelagic eggs from which they emerged. This brief embryonic phase and diminutive neonatal mass are characteristic of marine teleosts that produce numerous small, planktonic offspring as part of an opportunistic reproductive strategy.

Sexual maturation in Siganus guttatus proceeds in concert with somatic growth, culminating in the attainment of puberty at a specific body size. Field-collected specimens examined for gonadal development indicate that the total length at puberty is 27.3 centimeters [Lp = 27.3 centimeters]. Corresponding to this length threshold, the wet weight at puberty reaches approximately 383 grams [Wwp = approximately 383 grams]. Individuals at this stage exhibit clear signs of gonadal recrudescence and are capable of entering the spawning population. The relationship between length and maturity in this species aligns closely with patterns observed in other rabbitfishes, where a defined size window marks the transition from an immature, growing juvenile to a reproductively viable adult capable of contributing to the next generation.

Reproductive output in Siganus guttatus is substantial, with spawning events occurring throughout an extended breeding season under warm thermal regimes. Investigations at 28.7 °C [T = 28.7 °C] documented a maximum daily reproduction rate of approximately 1,695 eggs per day [Ri = approximately 1,695 eggs per day] for gravid females. This high fecundity is characteristic of many tropical siganids and is supported by the species' planktivorous feeding habits, which provide the necessary energetic resources for continuous gamete production. The daily rate of egg liberation, when considered over the duration of a spawning season, underscores the considerable reproductive potential of this species, which helps sustain its populations despite high levels of larval mortality in the planktonic environment.

The asymptotic body size of Siganus guttatus corresponds to an ultimate wet weight of 1598 grams [Wwi = 1598 grams], a value derived from length-weight regressions applied to the maximum recorded total length. Adults approaching this upper mass limit are typically older individuals that have completed most of their somatic growth. Under controlled aquarium conditions maintained at a temperature of 28.7 °C [T = 28.7 °C], the maximum lifespan of this species has been estimated at 2190 days [am = 2190 days], representing nearly six years of potential longevity. This lifespan is moderate for a teleost of its size and is consistent with an iteroparous life-history strategy, wherein adults spawn repeatedly across multiple breeding seasons before reaching senescence and eventual natural death.

Comparisons with related species provide useful context for the life-history parameters of Siganus guttatus. The maximum daily reproduction rate of approximately 1,695 eggs per day [Ri = approximately 1,695 eggs per day] observed in this species is comparable to that documented in the congeneric Siganus fuscescens under similar thermal regimes. The total length of 27.3 centimeters [Lp = 27.3 centimeters] at which puberty occurs corresponds to roughly 65 percent of the ultimate total length of 42 centimeters [Li = 42 centimeters], a proportional size at maturation consistent with many tropical marine fishes. The relatively brief incubation period of 2.5 days [ab = 2.5 days] and the minute wet weight at birth of 0.000087 grams [Wwb = 0.000087 grams] position Siganus guttatus firmly within the r-selected end of the life-history continuum, where high fecundity compensates for low per-offspring investment and substantial early-life mortality at a temperature of 28.7 °C [T = 28.7 °C].
